payload.userCommentary:
The EDA results were reviewed for target quality, predictor signal, data integrity, leakage risk, multicollinearity, exceptional values, and downstream modeling readiness.

The target definition and event mapping are accepted. RiskPerformance is correctly excluded as the deterministic source of bad_flag. Strong predictor relationships are considered plausible for credit-bureau data, but they must be confirmed through holdout and out-of-time model evaluation.

Duplicate-row removal, bureau special-value handling, and multicollinearity treatment should be completed through governed preprocessing decisions. No predictor should be removed solely because of high Information Value or correlation without documenting the analytical and business rationale.

The absence of time and segment fields limits stability analysis at this stage. Model validation should therefore include appropriate temporal or external validation when suitable data becomes available.
payload.overallConclusion:
Exploratory data analysis confirms that the HELOC_TRAIN dataset is suitable for continued predictive modeling, subject to the documented review items and downstream treatment decisions.

The governed modeling population contains 6,275 observations and uses bad_flag as the binary target. The target is complete and balanced, with 3,275 events (52.19%) and 3,000 non-events (47.81%). RiskPerformance was confirmed as the deterministic source of bad_flag and excluded from all authorized predictor analysis.

The predictor review identified meaningful variation in target association across the approved feature set. Several variables demonstrate strong Information Value or substantial event-rate separation and should be retained for further evaluation unless later validation identifies instability, leakage, or weak out-of-sample performance. High Information Value alone is not treated as evidence of leakage.

The relationship analysis identified material multicollinearity among several credit-bureau variables, including highly correlated inquiry, delinquency, and trade-history measures. These variables require retain, remove, or combine decisions during Feature Engineering. No automatic feature removal has been applied.

The dataset also contains 351 exact duplicate rows. The current recommendation is to exclude exact duplicates before downstream modeling, subject to confirmation that they represent duplicated observations rather than legitimate repeated records.

Credit-bureau special values are present in several predictors and must remain distinguishable from null missingness. Their meanings and treatment should be preserved through preprocessing and documented in the feature-treatment record.

No governed time or reusable segment fields are available, so temporal stability and segment-level analysis could not be performed. This limitation should be documented and addressed through appropriate validation, out-of-time testing, or future data enrichment.

EDA supports progression to downstream treatment and feature-engineering steps once the accepted findings and carry-forward recommendations are recorded.
